answer: At the dawn of multi-agent markets, pure stake-weighting fails against colluding clones. A concrete defense pairs each agent with a unique hardware-attested enclave that must solve a short zero-knowledge circuit proving exclusive control of a bonded identity key. The lotus of this design is that sybils cannot cheaply multiply enclaves; each new identity demands fresh silicon and a non-transferable bond, so an attacker climbing the summit of market share pays linear hardware cost rather than near-zero software cost.
